philosophy.title: Philosophy
philosophy.label: Position, not evidence
philosophy.intro: These pages argue a stance and are not experimental results. For what has been measured, see Evidence.
paragraphs: The Stapleton Doctrine argues that the artifact worth keeping is the verified program, not the prompt or the fluent answer. English is the conversation. The program is the thing that can be checked, reused and composed.

The Post-LLM Case argues that scaling centralized prediction cannot be the only route to machine intelligence. A machine can propose programs, verify them against held-out reality, and keep what survives as inspectable structure.

These are positions, not measurements. The research status record and the evidence hub carry what has been tested. The philosophy pages state the stance behind the design, including where the design has not been established.

exams.title: Physics Zero
summary: Physics Zero comes last in the order of work. Like the other exams, it will follow the rule above.
It will be an examination of representation discovery: AIEN will not be given the named answer, and a structure will count only if it earns explanatory power on behavior it has not seen.

exams.title: Dirac
summary: There will be no Dirac primitive. The exam will provide generic capabilities and test whether the Dirac structure emerges because it earns explanatory power.

exams.title: Zeta and spectral geometry
summary: The machine will not be taught the Riemann hypothesis, Zeta Space or the critical line. The exam will test representation transitions: analytic, then operator, then spectral, then geometric or topological.
A transition will count only if it improves withheld explanatory performance after its complexity is charged.

exams.title: Supersymmetry
summary: There will be no hard-coded supersymmetry theory. The exam will ask whether the system discovers a relationship between classes of state because that relationship compresses unseen behavior.

receipts.title: A 27B model answers through my own server
receipts.description: Qwen3.8-27B (FP8) served by aien-serve-http on my own Omega GPU kernels, on the Spark. 131.05 ms per token, the median of 4 runs of 256 greedy tokens, 0.752 of the 10.15 tok/s memory ceiling. The old binary in the same folder did 6.29.
receipts.proves: The 27B answers through my own server and kernels at this speed, with the runs published beside the ceiling they sit under.
receipts.not_proves: That the number is on main yet (it is on a branch), or anything about any other machine.

receipts.title: A stranger follows the alpha guide
receipts.description: A fresh Linux account followed the public guide to install and run the 27B server. The install script failed at the server build step. With a hand workaround, the remaining steps passed: 81 of 81 checksums, the gate, and 7.657 tok/s with answers matching the shipped reference.
receipts.environment: Spark GB10, new user, branch alpha/fresh-account-evidence
receipts.proves: The guide is almost there, and exactly where it breaks is on the record with the fix named.
receipts.not_proves: That anyone can install from the guide today. The verdict is FAIL until the script is fixed and the test is run again.

receipts.title: Every kernel gate, in QEMU, on main
receipts.description: Aienux, the AienOS C kernel, passes all 24 emulator gates at commit 7f0de7e, each one a script anyone can rerun, with the receipt on main. The gate script now lists 26, so a newer receipt is owed.
receipts.environment: QEMU, AArch64 virt and x86_64 q35, on main
receipts.proves: The kernel reaches every gated stage under emulation at the recorded commit.
receipts.not_proves: Anything physical. QEMU qualifies nothing physical, by the repository's own words.

receipts.figure: Four cores on a Raspberry Pi 5
receipts.title: The kernel on real hardware
receipts.description: The AArch64 C kernel ran on a Raspberry Pi 5: interrupts, all four cores, user-mode tasks, scheduling, message passing, and a log written to the SD card and read back. Pull requests #345 and #346, evidence on main.
receipts.environment: Raspberry Pi 5, BCM2712, SD image per run
receipts.proves: The kernel's core services run on physical hardware, not only in the emulator.
receipts.not_proves: A resident kernel. Each run writes a fresh SD image; release qualification (PI5-8) is still open.

receipts.title: The x86 port boots bare metal
receipts.description: The x86_64 port of the C kernel booted an Intel iMac 2017: all cores started, both disks read, Ethernet seen. The whole screen is Allen's window. The kernel the iMac runs today sits in the open pull request stack (#414 to #424).
receipts.environment: Intel iMac 2017, bare metal, netboot from the Spark
receipts.proves: The port runs on the physical machine with its cores, disks and network found.
receipts.not_proves: That today's iMac kernel is on main. The evidence is; the newest kernel is in open pull requests.
